extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word if exposed to the whole passage but not if only the last sentence is visible. The dataset exemplifies a wide range of linguistic phenomena and challenges models to understand broader discourse context.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. In Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers) (pp. 1525–1534).
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The LAMBADA dataset was constructed from the Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), which contains unpublished novels. The data collection process involved filtering passages to ensure the target word was guessable only with broad discourse context, not local sentence context. This was achieved using a combination of language models and human evaluation via CrowdFlower crowdsourcing. Passages were excluded if any language model assigned a probability ≥0.00175 to the target word. Human subjects then evaluated the remaining passages in three steps: guessing the target word with the full passage, verifying with another subject, and ensuring the word could not be guessed from the last sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels (5,325 novels and 465 million words).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was constructed from the Book Corpus, which includes novels published prior to 2016. The exact timeframe of novel publication is not specified, but the dataset was released in 2016.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Passages were filtered to exclude those where the target word had a probability ≥0.00175 according to any of four language models. The remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects to ensure the target word could only be guessed with broad discourse context, not local sentence context. Only passages passing all selection steps were included in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects guessed the target word based on the full passage (context + target sentence) in two steps, followed by a third step where subjects guessed the word based on the target sentence alone. Only passages where two consecutive subjects matched the missing word and no subject could guess it from the local context were included.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process ensured that the target word could only be guessed with broad discourse context. Passages were discarded if the target word was guessable from the last sentence alone, even with multiple guesses. The strict criteria required two consecutive subjects to match the missing word exactly.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2-3 human annotations per item (two for full passage, one or more for sentence-only context).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models (pre-trained RNN, 4-gram model, RNN, and feed-forward model) were used to filter passages based on target word probability.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are available for download. The test set is planned for release during a public competition. Versioning and deprecation policies are not explicitly mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to evaluate language models' ability to understand broader discourse context, which is crucial for applications requiring deep text comprehension. It highlights the limitations of current models in capturing non-local phenomena.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward proper nouns (48% of target words), which are overrepresented compared to other parts of speech. The target word or its lemma often appears in the context (over 80% of LAMBADA passages), facilitating co-reference resolution. Direct speech is more frequent in LAMBADA items (71%) than in the input data (61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to narrative passages from novels, which may not generalize to other text genres. The strict filtering criteria may exclude linguistically interesting cases. The dataset is designed to be challenging for language models, and its difficulty may limit its use for training models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of language models for broad discourse context understanding. The dataset is not intended for training models but for benchmarking their ability to handle non-local phenomena in natural language text.
